chapter_name: Yoga for Holistic Health and Personal Excellence
learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the ancient Indian science of Yoga. Learn how physical postures, breath control, and meditation combine to build a stress-free mind and a healthy body!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Yuj', meaning to join or unite. It is the union of the individual soul with the universal spirit. It brings harmony between mind, body, and emotions.

Patanjali described 8 limbs of Yoga: Yama (social ethics), Niyama (personal discipline), Asana (postures), Pranayama (breath control), Pratyahara (sense withdrawal), Dharana (concentration), Dhyana (meditation), and Samadhi (salvation).

Asanas are physical postures designed to improve flexibility, strength, and internal organ function. They can be meditative (Padmasana), relaxing (Shavasana), or corrective (Bhujangasana for posture).

Pranayama is the regulation of breath (inhalation, retention, exhalation). It calms the nervous system. Dhyana (Meditation) is a continuous flow of concentration, which reduces stress and improves focus.
Regular Yoga practice is highly effective in preventing and managing modern lifestyle diseases like obesity, diabetes, hypertension, back pain, and asthma.

fun_activity.title: 🌬️ The 4-7-8 Breathing Trick
fun_activity.instructions: Try this simple Pranayama technique to instantly relax: Inhale quietly through your nose for 4 seconds, hold your breath for 7 seconds, and exhale completely through your mouth for 8 seconds. Repeat 3 times!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the 8 limbs of Ashtanga Yoga in the exact sequence.
📌 Distinguish between Yama (rules for interacting with society) and Niyama (rules for personal discipline).
📌 Learn at least two Asanas (e.g., Tadasana, Vajrasana) that help in curing specific diseases like Obesity or Back Pain.
quick_recap: ⭐ Yoga is not a religion; it is a scientific way of living a healthy and balanced life.
⭐ Asanas should be performed with deep breathing and a relaxed mind, not forcefully.
⭐ International Day of Yoga is celebrated worldwide on June 21st to highlight its universal benefits.
